improvementsForA: The ground is a single flat olive-mustard fill with faint noise; there is no grass, no texture, no light falloff that reads as terrain. Replace it with an actual meadow surface (grass tufts, flowers, mowed-path value variation) — right now it reads as a UI background color, not a place.

Nothing casts a shadow: cards, the fence, and every perimeter rock/tree float on the ground plane. Add grounded contact shadows with one consistent sun direction; the fence in the top-left corner especially looks pasted on.

The perimeter 'environment' is unresolved: the corner crops (bl, br, tr) are abstract near-black and mud-brown polyhedra with no material identity — I could not tell rocks from bushes from trees. Give them albedo/lighting so they read as foliage and stone, and vary silhouettes.

Cards have zero edge thickness — they are flat rectangles. The hand cards also show a teal under-border sticking out on one side like a misregistered layer; either make that an intentional sleeve with even margins or remove it.

The stream in field-corner-tl/br is a hard-edged cyan ribbon with three flat bands and aliased edges; it looks like a masking-tape strip. It needs banks, softened edges, and lighting consistent with the scene.

The center divider is a clean glow line, but it sits on featureless ground so it reads as an HTML hr with bloom. Once the terrain is real, let the seam interact with it (scorched/blessed grass, irregular falloff) instead of a perfectly uniform gradient.
improvementsForB: The rules text on every card face is pseudo-glyph gibberish (rows of diamond/circle symbols) — beautiful frames, unreadable game surfaces. Replace with real typeset card text; this is the single biggest blocker to shipping and the one axis where the other render is clearly ahead.
Heavy bloom/haze washes out the top-left quadrant (field-corner-tl is nearly overexposed and milky); pull the atmospheric glow back so the stream and fence keep local contrast.

Corner detail crops are soft and smeary — the bl/tr trees and rocks look like an upscaled painting with lost edges. A pass of crisper texture (grass blade detail, harder rock facets) at native resolution would remove the 'AI upscale' feel.
The divider seam's edge is wobbly with small crackle artifacts and an unexplained truncated glowing rectangle near its lower-left; clean the seam path and remove the stray glow fragment.

Card-face iconography (the stat rows and crest symbols) is mushy at gameplay scale; the 18-heart and some medallions show speckled artifacts. Tighten these UI elements as crisp vector overlays composited over the painterly board rather than baked into it.
The two rows read slightly differently in saturation (player row cooler/greener than the sunwashed opponent row); a light grade unification would lock the two halves into one continuous meadow.
notes: B reads as an actual sunlit meadow: textured grass with flowers, one coherent warm sun with long cast shadows, decks and cards that have real edge thickness and contact shadows, and a stream with believable water. A is a flat mustard plane ringed by unlit black polyhedra — clean and legible, but it looks like a diagram, not a place; it loses every environment crop outright. B's decisive flaw is that all card text is illegible pseudo-glyphs and its detail crops are soft, but those are finishing problems on top of a shippable foundation, whereas A's problems are foundational.
